elements.element: Customer has a unilateral right to terminate for convenience, including during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language permits Customer to terminate for convenience “at any time, including during the Initial Period.”

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience is effective on 30 days' advance notice.
elements.evidence: The added language requires not less than 90 days' prior notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly requires notice “in writing.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is provided. The existing denial of credit for capital costs does not satisfy this refund requirement.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right effective during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language states that Vendor may terminate for convenience “only effective at the end of the then-current term.”

elements.element: Customer has a unilateral right to terminate for convenience, including during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language permits Customer to terminate for convenience “at any time, including during the Initial Period.”

elements.element: Customer's required advance-notice period for termination for convenience is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires not less than 90 days' prior notice, which implements the permitted 90-day endpoint.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable because of Customer's termination for convenience does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that any such fee “shall not exceed three (3) months' fees.”
The added language expressly states that Vendor “may terminate for convenience.”

elements.element: Vendor's termination for convenience may be effective only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Although the addition says Vendor may terminate “only effective at the end of the then-current term,” retained Section 18.1 permits “any Party,” which includes Vendor, to terminate at the end of the Initial Period “or any time thereafter.” The provisions conflict, and “then-current term” is not defined for the post-Initial Period.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 90 days' advance notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language requires Vendor to give “not less than 90 days' prior written notice.”

result.reason: The addition substantially tracks the fallback and does not meet the preferred 30-day notice or pro-rata refund requirements. It does not securely complete the fallback because the retained generic right allowing any Party to terminate at any time after the Initial Period conflicts with the new restriction limiting Vendor termination to a term end. A conforming edit to Section 18.1, and preferably clarification of “then-current term,” is required.
